turns.assistant_text:
Dưới đây là những tin tức nổi bật về AI hôm nay:

1. **[Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/ai-health-advice-accuracy-messaging-risk-behavioral-benchmarking)**: AI đang cung cấp hướng dẫn sức khỏe với quy mô chưa từng có, nhưng có những rủi ro liên quan đến việc AI có thể gây hại nếu không được kiểm soát đúng cách. Chính phủ đang xem xét việc tích hợp AI vào chăm sóc sức khỏe để giao tiếp trực tiếp với bệnh nhân.

2. **[Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?](https://theconversation.com/why-is-nvidia-so-powerful-in-the-ai-world-and-what-could-jensen-huangs-scandal-really-cost-296257)**: Nvidia là một trong những công ty chủ chốt trong ngành AI, nhưng đang đối mặt với những lo ngại về khả năng sinh lời trong tương lai. Sự thống trị của Nvidia trong thị trường chip AI đang bị thách thức bởi các công ty khác như Google và AMD.

3. **[Banks push online banking, then blame us when we get hacked | Opinion](https://www.usatoday.com/story/opinion/columnist/2026/11/10/ai-online-banking-vulnerable-hacking/92588938007)**: Bài viết này bàn về sự lo ngại của con người đối với AI và cách mà chúng ta đang dần giao phó quyền kiểm soát cho máy móc trong cuộc sống hàng ngày.

4. **[AI is making it harder to detect fake emergency calls : NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/nx-s1-5971477/ai-is-making-it-harder-to-detect-fake-emergency-calls)**: AI đang làm cho việc phát hiện các cuộc gọi khẩn cấp giả mạo trở nên khó khăn hơn, với việc công nghệ này được sử dụng để tạo ra các cuộc gọi giả mạo đến cơ quan chức năng.

5. **[AI stocks bounce back — with one notable exception](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/10/ai-stocks-nvidia-broadcom)**: Thị trường cổ phiếu AI đã phục hồi, mặc dù Nvidia đang gặp khó khăn sau những tiết lộ về CEO của họ. Các nhà đầu tư đang theo dõi sát sao tình hình này.

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by [...] Many health communicators assume that those who learn the facts will pursue healthier choices. AI is now being built on the same assumption, which ignores how messages actually influence behavior. Messages, like medicines, can help, harm, or do nothing at all, and the only way to know which is to test them.

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.title: Banks push online banking, then blame us when we get hacked | Opinion
items.summary:
People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives. [...] One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] For that matter, we're starting to trust AI to give us authoritative answers to all of life's questions, including those where human moral judgments and lived experiences might guide us better.

After all, why bother doing any research on our own when we can just type a question into a search field and have some chatbot spit out a near-instantaneous response?

items.title: AI stocks bounce back — with one notable exception
items.summary:
The AI trade has regained momentum despite — or maybe because of — Nvidia's struggles following the weekend revelations from CEO Jensen Huang.

The big picture: Monday's sudden burst of exuberance for AI was the latest wide swing for a market upended by last week's "blue tsunami" in the midterm elections and the threat they could pose to the data center boom. [...] For example, even before the news about the Nvidia CEO or the anti-data center vote at the polls, Wall Street expectations for capital expenditures from hyperscalers had been looking a bit flat.
   Given that a large percentage of that AI investment is spent on the semiconductors needed to make these computing centers, well, compute, that would seem to be important for tech investors.

What's next:Will the stock market's rally be the start of a new phase of AI exuberance? [...] Hyperscalers rose, paced by Meta, which notched a gain of 5.1%. 
   Semiconductors roared, with the SOX index posting its best gain — 6.9% — since late July. 

Yes, but: The glaring exception to the AI-palooza was its best-known player, Nvidia.

   Weekend revelations from CEO Jensen Huang — who acknowledged having an affair with a woman suspected of connections to Chinese intelligence — left investors grappling with uncertainty about the CEO's future.
